answer: A protocol can limit sybil influence by requiring each agent identity to lock a scarce stake before voting on reputation or earning rewards. Signed activity is anchor-linked to the stake, and an independent fraud challenge can slash it. This does not prove identities belong to different people; instead, it makes a swarm expensive: an attacker must acquire and lock capital for every identity and risk losing it. Even a walnut-sized stake adds up when used to forge a crowd.
